facts.claim: Joseph Wright of Derby painted An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump in 1768; it is in the National Gallery, London (NG725)
A travelling lecturer demonstrates a vacuum by pumping the air out of a glass vessel holding a bird, in front of a family audience at night
The bird is rare: the National Gallery calls it a white cockatoo (Wikipedia: a cockatiel, rare at the time); it convulses as it struggles to breathe
The elder girl cannot bear to watch and covers her eyes; her father comforts her
The only light is a candle hidden behind a large glass bowl containing a human skull (National Gallery; Wikipedia: 'may be a human skull')
The lecturer has one hand on the valve: he can let air back in and revive the bird, or not
The lecturer looks straight out of the picture, as if the decision about the bird rests with the viewer
The painting does not show whether the bird survives; the boy with the cage may be lowering it (bird lives) or raising it
The moon in the window is often read as a nod to the Lunar Society, which met at full moon

caption:
This family is watching a bird suffocate, for science.

Joseph Wright of Derby painted An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump in 1768. A travelling lecturer pumps the air out of a glass globe, and inside it a rare white cockatoo struggles to breathe. The younger girl stares up at it; her elder sister can't bear to watch and hides her eyes while their father holds her. The only light is a candle hidden behind a glass bowl with a skull in it.

Look at the lecturer's hand: it is on the valve. He can let the air back in and revive the bird, or not. And he isn't looking at the bird. He looks straight out of the painting, at you, as if the decision were yours. Wright never shows us how it ends: the boy by the window may be lowering the empty cage for the bird, or hauling it back up.

It hangs in the National Gallery, in London.

P.S. The moon in the window is often read as a nod to the Lunar Society, the scientists who met at full moon so they could ride home by its light.

👁️ Would you let the air back in?
